source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of the exact original XML verse substring, including written/read notes, not a normalized substitute.
source.public_versification_note: Public 7:1–25 = Hebrew 7:1–25; public 8:1–4 = Hebrew 7:26–29; public 8:5–32 = Hebrew 8:1–28.

key_decisions.decision: Binds public 8:1 to Hebrew 7:26 and preserves the renewed message with its serving purpose; nested speech continues through verse 4.
Binds to Hebrew 7:27 and retains the conditional refusal and complete territorial scope without adding a natural mechanism.
Binds to Hebrew 7:28 and retains every location, from royal bed to food preparation, and the repeated into movement.
Binds to Hebrew 7:29 and preserves the bodily invasion as well as all three affected groups.
Preserves the magicians’ multiplication of the affliction rather than treating their action as its removal.
Renders the unusual honor-over-me idiom as granting the timing choice while keeping all beneficiaries and the Nile exception.
Keeps Moses as the one crying out; uses a passive for the relative clause whose Hebrew subject is not named rather than deciding silently between divine and mediated agency.
Preserves Pharaoh as the explicit hardening agent after relief, unlike the uncaused grammatical descriptions in 7:13 and 7:22.
Retains dust as the transformed material and gnats as a conventional but uncertain identification of the insect term.
Distinguishes the unsuccessful attempt from earlier successes and keeps animals within the account’s harm.
Retains the finger image and conventional God rendering while noting that the magicians use elohim rather than the divine name; no conversion is inferred.
Retains the send/release word connection and all affected places while noting that flies is an uncertain identification of the swarm term.
Keeps the specifically stated distinction for Goshen and the spatial claim, with earth as an alternative sense of land noted.
Retains the Masoretic redemption noun through redeeming rather than silently replacing it with a different Hebrew word for distinction; makes the between-people relation readable.
Keeps the LORD’s action, royal and servant households, and the strong land-ruin description without adding a disease diagnosis.
Keeps abomination as a culturally attributed claim and the threatened stoning, with the alternative relation to Egyptian sacred animals noted rather than specified in the text.
Keeps the timing and Moses’ shift to Pharaoh in the third person, preserving the force of the warning against renewed deception.
Retains Pharaoh as the explicit agent and this-time-too repetition, ending the episode with unfulfilled release.
